description: Run Photoshop's Sky Replacement (Adobe Sensei): detect the sky, composite a replacement, and relight/colour-grade the foreground to match. Non-destructive — everything lands in a "Sky Replacement Group" of editable layers above the original, so the result can be tuned or deleted afterwards. Pick one of Photoshop's built-in skies by name with sky (no path needed; sky "list" names them), or pass sky_file with an ABSOLUTE path to ANY image on disk; with neither, Photoshop's Blue Sky 001 is used (or the first installed sky). Reach for harmonization_opacity and foreground_lighting_opacity when the composite reads as pasted-on; those two carry most of the believability. Fails cleanly when the image has no detectable sky (indoor or closed compositions).

border_smoothness.description: Softens the boundary between sky and foreground. 0 is a hard cut.

brightness.description: Brightness of the replaced sky itself.

edge_lighting_opacity.description: Strength of the light wrap along the foreground edge where it meets the sky.

foreground_lighting_opacity.description: Strength of the relighting applied to the foreground so it appears lit by the new sky.

harmonization_opacity.description: How strongly the foreground is colour-graded to match the new sky. This is what sells the composite — 0 leaves the foreground untouched and usually reads as pasted-on.

shift_edge.description: Moves the sky/foreground boundary inward (negative) or outward (positive). Use it when the horizon leaves a halo or eats into the foreground.

sky.description: Name of one of Photoshop's built-in skies, e.g. "Blue Sky 002", "Spectacular 004" or "Sunset Sky 003" (skies the user saved in Photoshop work too). The server finds the image itself, so no file or folder access is needed. Pass "list" to get the installed skies' names without changing the document. Omit both sky and sky_file to use Photoshop's Blue Sky 001 (or the first installed sky).

sky_file.description: ABSOLUTE path to any image to use as the sky instead of a built-in one; it does not need to be a Photoshop sky preset. Takes precedence over sky.

sky_name.description: Label recorded on the operation. Cosmetic — it does not select the sky. Defaults to the built-in sky's name, or "Custom Sky" for sky_file.

temperature.description: Warms (positive) or cools (negative) the replaced sky.

name: ps_replace_sky

group_layers.description: Layers inside the group, top to bottom — typically the sky layer, an edge-lighting group, a foreground-lighting layer and a foreground-colour curves layer.

group_name.description: Name of the layer group Photoshop created.

skies.description: Installed sky names; returned instead of a composite when sky is "list".
